chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding two men who shared in wealth, profited from it, and where there was a debt against the wealth and a debt upon both of them; one said to his partner, 'Give me the capital, and for you is the profit, and upon you is the charge.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it if they stipulate it. If the stipulation opposes the Book of Allah, then it is returned to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.رَدٌّ إِلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: Returned to the Book of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on asymmetric division of capital, profit, and debt in a partnership?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates an asymmetric partnership agreement where one partner takes the capital and profit while the other assumes the debt, provided it is mutually stipulated. This ruling illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *al-shart* (the condition), where specific contractual stipulations are binding unless they explicitly contradict the clear text of the Quran, in which case the divine law prevails. The narration underscores the flexibility of commercial jurisprudence (*Fiqh al-Mu'amalat*) within the bounds of Shariah, emphasizing that private agreements are subordinate to divine commandments.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding two men who participated in some merchandise, and there was a profit in it, and there was a debt (a charge) against the merchandise, and upon both of them is a debt. So one of the two said to his companions, ‘Give me the capital of the wealth and for you is the profit made, and upon you would be the charge (on the asset)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it when it is stipulated. So if the stipulation opposes the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so it is returned to the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ’Umayr from Hammad from af-Halabiy from abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, who has said the following:

"This is about the two men who had a business partnership with a certain amount of asset in which they made a certain amount of profit, there, however, was a loan against that asset which both had to pay. One of them asked the other to give him the capital in exchange for the profit and payment of loan. The Imam said, ‘There is no offense in such deal provided they had established such condition, however, if the condition is against the book of Allah it then is a rejection of the book of Allah.’"
